posts.title: Why we need to ditch “temporary disability” in inclusive design
posts.description: Summary: If you do accessibility work or talks, stop treating Microsoft’s “temporary disability” as a kind of disability. Microsoft Inclusive Design’s “temporary or situational disabilities” are not legal disabilities. A broken wrist ends; systemic access barriers don’t. posts.description: Summary: Defaults in design are not simple shortcuts or starting points. They carry design decisions, bias and assumptions about what users need and want moment-to-moment.
